english: Referral of Children to the Health Facility
When to refer a child, signs of allergy, and the referral steps.
In the field — a CDD explains a referral to a caregiver, holding the referral form.
When to refer a sick child
A child is sick or has danger signs when the child has:
Convulsion.
Fever or high temperature.
Difficulty breathing.
Difficulty staying awake.
Vomiting.
Not able to eat or drink.
Severe pains or bleeding.
Neck pain or severe headache.
Severe Acute Malnutrition.
Do refer the child when the child is sick or has danger signs.
Do refer the child when the child has fever.
Why refer?
Children with fever may have malaria or other childhood infections.
Malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea are the leading causes of death in under-five children in Nigeria.
Children with fever need evaluation to avoid complications.
Children with SAM after MUAC screening are excluded, evaluated and given support (resuscitation, feeding programme, etc.).
Allergy and side effects
Step 1
Allergies to AZM are rare but may occur.
Step 2
Refer a child to the nearest health facility if the child has side effects or suspected adverse reactions.
Do refer a child who shows any of these signs after AZM.
Do not give AZM to a child with any of these signs. Refer the child.
Possible allergy or reasons for exclusion
Swelling of the face, mouth, tongue or other parts of the body.
Nausea or continuous vomiting.
Skin rashes or blistering of the skin.
Body itching.
Weakness or fatigue.
Loss of appetite.
Abdominal pains, diarrhoea.
Headache.
Yellowing of the skin or eyes.
Referral steps
Use these steps for children who are sick, have severe acute malnutrition or have suspected adverse reactions.
Step — do not give AZM, fill the referral form, then explain the referral to the caregiver.
Do not give AZM.
Complete the top portion of the referral form.
Explain the reason for the referral and the need to act immediately.
Tell the caregiver how to get to the nearest health facility.
Give the AZM referral form to the caregiver to take to the health facility.
Explain the danger
Explain the danger
If the child has fever or SAM, the child could have malaria or other diseases. Explain that the child could get worse or die without immediate treatment.
Explain that the health worker will evaluate the child at the facility.
Key take away of module 3
Key take away of module 3

1. Refer children who are sick or malnourished to the nearest health facility. 2. Fill out the referral form and give it to the caregiver to take to the health facility. 3. Explain the reason for referral and encourage the caregiver to take the child to the health facility immediately.
